summary: Combined Pinpoint content verification is not revision-scoped on the engine handoff path, so import-finished and content-contains can disagree about which revision was checked. The fake search surface also collapses multi-document matches into a single per-import hit count.

findings.summary: Combined handoff omits revisionNumber, so new content-contains checks are not tied to the revision whose import just finished.
findings.rationale: `#revisionTarget` returns only `{ libraryId, publicationId, revisionId }`. `verifyRevision` → `contentContains` therefore omits `?revisionNumber=…`. Import status is keyed by revisionId, but the fake content handler (and real content API without a revision filter) can serve another COMPLETED revision of the same publication (`candidates.at(-1)`). This change makes content/search assertions load-bearing on that path; adapter unit tests pass `revisionNumber: 1` manually, but the engine never does.

findings.summary: Fake ftsSearch numFound counts matching imports, not matching documents.
findings.rationale: A job contributes at most `+1` when any document text includes the keyword, even if several documents match. Adapter `search-finds` compares `minHits` to `numFound`, so expectations like `minHits: 2` against one multi-document package can never pass on the fake while still looking like a green orchestration proof for `minHits: 1`. That collapses document-level hit cardinality into publication/import presence.

findings.summary: Deferring every expectedOutput as search-finds reports success as “no expectedOutputs”.
findings.rationale: With `deferSearchFinds` and a fixture that only has `search-finds`, `checkable` is empty and the function returns a passing `output-package` assertion claiming there were no expectations. Deferred is collapsed into absent; consumers of the assertion list cannot tell search was intentionally skipped for Pinpoint.
